t: Try square - Wikipedia
s: July 18, 2025 - Typically the blade and the stock will be rectangular in profile, though on some wooden squares the ends of the blade and the stock might be cut to a decorative shape. Some steel blades also have ruler markings for making measurements. Often the top of the stock will not cover the full width of the blade so the stock does not get in the way when making a mark. This gap also allows space should an inaccurate blade need to be planed, filed or sanded. Try squares are typically 3 to 24 inches (76 to 610 mm) long.
